sound: Checked and correct: link safety (isSafeUrl/safeHref in makeFinding, cleanModelText and cleanData). Model text drops markup and images. The quick brief cleans every result before ranking and cleans its assembled brief. Redaction runs before clipping, and a clipped tail of digits is dropped. gradeText is cleaned. The Companies House registered office is kept and personal or service addresses are removed. Emails, US and UK phones, US streets, P.O. boxes, infobox birth lines and 'Masayoshi Son founded SoftBank' all behave correctly. The cleaners ran adversarial 4,000-character inputs in under 10 ms. The temporary test was deleted.

findings.title: A whole court or DOJ record is deleted when its title mentions H-1B, a green card, political contributions or a diagnosis, so a conviction disappears and the subject looks clean
findings.scenario: sanitizeFinding({source:'doj-press-releases', category:'regulatory', title:'Silicon Valley CEO sentenced for H-1B visa fraud scheme', ...}) returned null. Three more DOJ records also returned null: a quote saying 'promised investors a path to a green card through the EB-5 program', one saying 'illegal political contributions through straw donors', and one saying 'Patients were diagnosed with conditions they did not have'. An FDA recall quote saying 'Three patients were hospitalized' also returned null. The conviction never reaches the report.
findings.fix: For OFFICIAL_SOURCES records, skip the title check, or apply only the minor and personal-details rules to it. In their quotes, judge immigration, politics and health against the subject's own private status (visa status, donations, illness), not against crimes or schemes. A matter about fraud, convictions, charges or patients is never removed. Add these five records as regression tests.
findings.evidence: Temporary jest probe through sanitizeFinding: 4 of 5 DOJ records were null, and the FDA recall was null.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: all five DOJ/FDA records returned null from sanitizeFinding. Line 530 drops the record if its title matches any protected rule, whatever the source. H-1B fraud and straw-donor crimes are not the person's immigration status or donation record.
findings.betterFix: Do not exempt official sources wholesale, because a court record about someone's own health must still go. Scope the patterns: IMMIGRATION, POLITICS and HEALTH_ALWAYS do not match when the sentence has an enforcement term (fraud, sentenced, charged, convicted, scheme, illegal, straw) or a third-party object (patients, investors). For official records, redact a private title rather than nulling the record. Add the five records as regressions.

findings.title: HEALTH_ALWAYS and HEALTH_PERSON remove company facts about health companies: 'pregnant', 'diagnosed', 'hospitalized', 'treated for' and 'after a COVID…'
findings.scenario: cleanSentences dropped each of these as 'health': 'Maven Clinic serves pregnant women and new parents', 'Ro sells medication to pregnant patients', 'Theranos tests led some patients to be wrongly diagnosed', 'patients were treated for conditions they did not have', 'Sales collapsed after a COVID-19 lockdown in 2020', 'Their COVID response won praise', 'Acme has diabetes customers', 'Cerebral faced a probe over drug use'. A title such as 'Maven Clinic CEO Kate Ryder: supporting pregnant workers' nulls the whole record. Health-company founders get thin profiles.
findings.fix: Make HEALTH_ALWAYS terms (pregnant, diagnosed, hospitalized, treated for, drug use) person-bound. Remove them only when a pronoun or the subject is the one affected ('she is pregnant', 'he was hospitalized'). Do not remove them when the object is patients, women, members, customers or users. Add lockdown, response, restrictions, customers, members and patients to HEALTH_BUSINESS. Test with Maven, Hinge, Theranos and Cerebral sentences.
findings.evidence: Temporary jest probe: 9 company sentences dropped, and the Maven title finding was null.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: the Maven, Theranos, COVID-lockdown, 'diabetes customers' and Cerebral drug-use sentences were all dropped as health. HEALTH_ALWAYS matches pregnant, diagnosed and drug use with no person tie.
findings.betterFix: Tie HEALTH_ALWAYS terms to a person (a pronoun or the subject, plus is/was). Exempt plural third-party objects (patients, women, customers, members, users). Add lockdown(s), restrictions, response and customers to HEALTH_BUSINESS. Keep regressions for true person cases such as 'she was diagnosed with'.

findings.title: SEXUALITY matches 'gay' and 'queer' anywhere, without regard to case, so a person named Gay gets an empty report and LGBTQ health companies lose their records
findings.scenario: Two inputs came back null: makeFinding for subject Gay Gaddis (T3) with title 'Gay Gaddis, founder of T3, on building an agency', and the quick brief's cleanSearchResult for 'Gay Gaddis - T3 founder'. Every record about her goes. 'Folx Health is a healthcare startup for queer and transgender people' and 'The Gay Area Youth Coalition gave Acme an award' are also dropped.
findings.fix: Remove sexuality only when the text is about a person: 'is/was/came out as gay', 'openly gay', 'his/her (same-sex) partner'. Use case-sensitive lowercase 'gay' or require a person verb, and never match a capitalised 'Gay' followed by a capitalised word (a name). Do not remove a sentence where the word describes the people a company serves ('for queer and transgender people').
findings.evidence: Probe: the Gay Gaddis finding was null in both the deep check and the quick brief, and the Folx sentence was dropped.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: 'Gay Gaddis, founder of T3...' was dropped as sexuality. SEXUALITY is case-insensitive with a bare 'gay', so every record about a person named Gay is removed. The Folx company sentence is dropped too.
findings.betterFix: Match bare gay, queer and lesbian only in lowercase and only after a person verb or descriptor (is/was/came out as/openly, 'gay man/woman'). Never match a capitalised Gay before a capitalised word. Do not match 'for queer and transgender people/patients'. Add a regression for the subject's own name.

findings.title: A private relative is kept when the subject's own role comes later in the sentence ('whose wife Carrie … is the founder of Nikola')
findings.scenario: cleanSentences kept 'Milton, whose wife Carrie is often at his side, is the founder of Nikola.' whole, and also kept 'He met his wife Sarah at Stanford, where he founded his first startup.' privateRelative tests PUBLIC_ROLE against the next 140 characters after the kin word. The 'founder' or 'founded' there belongs to the subject, not the relative, so the private spouse's name is shown. This breaks rule 3.
findings.fix: Count a role only when it is attached to the relative: in apposition right after the kin word or the relative's name (', a director of X', 'Bob Roe, CEO of'), or with the relative as subject ('her father runs/is CEO of'). End the clause at ', is', ', was', ', where', ', who' and the subject's own verbs. Do not count a role verb whose subject is he, she or the founder.
findings.evidence: Probe: both sentences came back unchanged from cleanSentences.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: both sentences came back unchanged. The PUBLIC_ROLE window after the kin word picks up the subject's own 'is the founder' and 'he founded'. CLAUSE_END has no ', is', ', where' or ', who'. The private spouse's name is shown, which breaks rule 3.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. End the clause at a comma followed by is/was/where/who/which, and at a pronoun subject (he/she). Count a role only when it is in apposition to the relative or the relative is its subject.

findings.title: Common health phrasings still get through: 'undergo treatment for cancer', 'his long battle with depression', 'a psychiatric hospital'
findings.scenario: cleanSentences kept 'Doe stepped down as CEO in 2021 to undergo treatment for cancer.', 'She took a leave of absence to undergo treatment for breast cancer.', 'He has been open about his long battle with depression.' and 'Doe spent time at a psychiatric hospital.' unchanged. They are shown in the quote and sent to the model.
findings.fix: In HEALTH_VERB, change 'treatment for (?:his|her|their)' to 'treatment for' followed by HEALTH_MOD. Add 'undergo/undergoing/underwent treatment' and 'battle with' (without a possessive). Allow up to 4 words between the possessive and the term when the words include battle, fight or struggle with. Add psychiatric (hospital|ward|facility|care) to HEALTH_ALWAYS.
findings.evidence: Probe: all four sentences came back with removed {}.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: all four sentences were kept, so a cancer treatment, depression and a psychiatric hospital reach the page and the model. This is a direct leak under rule 3, so it is more serious than medium.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Use 'treatment for' plus HEALTH_MOD plus HEALTH_TERM, and add undergo/undergoing/underwent treatment. Use a possessive plus up to 4 words when they include battle/fight/struggle with. Add psychiatric (hospital|ward|facility|unit|care) and 'mental health facility' to HEALTH_ALWAYS.

findings.title: MINOR's case-insensitive 'their … son' and 'son, <number>' remove sentences about Masayoshi Son (and drop whole records when the match is in a title)
findings.scenario: For subject Masayoshi Son, these were dropped as 'minor': 'SoftBank shareholders grilled their chairman Son over the losses.' and 'Son, 12 years after founding SoftBank, bought Vodafone Japan.' A title of that shape nulls the whole finding. KIN was made case-sensitive, but MINOR has the /i flag, so 'Son' as a surname still matches.
findings.fix: Split MINOR into a case-sensitive part for the kin nouns. Lowercase son, daughter and child for the '(his|her|their) (word)? son' and 'son, <age>' branches. Keep /i only for phrases such as 'kindergarten' and 'custody battle'. Add Masayoshi Son and Son Heung-min regressions.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: both Masayoshi Son sentences were dropped as minor. KIN is case-sensitive but MINOR has the /i flag, so a capitalised surname Son matches 'their chairman Son' and 'Son, 12'. A title of that shape nulls the record.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Make the son, daughter and child branches of MINOR case-sensitive and lowercase, and keep /i only for phrase branches. Add Masayoshi Son and Son Heung-min regressions, including a title.

findings.title: Company facts dropped as immigration or religion: H-1B sponsorship, deportation contracts, 'mission-critical'
findings.scenario: These were dropped: 'Palantir's software has been used by ICE in deportation operations.' (immigration), 'The company sponsored H-1B visas for 300 engineers.' (immigration), 'The software served a mission-critical function for the Navy.' (religion, via 'served a mission\b'), and 'She chairs a Jewish family foundation that funds hospitals.' The rule is meant for the person's own status or faith.
findings.fix: Match IMMIGRATION only for the person's own status (pronoun or name with 'is/was on', 'came on', 'obtained', 'applied for' plus visa or green card; 'was undocumented'; 'faced deportation'). Never match company, contract or program nouns. In RELIGION_PRACTICE, require '(?!-)' after 'mission'. Do not match 'a Jewish/Christian family foundation'.
findings.evidence: Probe: each sentence returned an empty text.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: all four company or third-party sentences were dropped (deport, H-1B, 'served a mission' before a hyphen, 'a Jewish family foundation').
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Tie IMMIGRATION to the person's own status. Exclude sponsor(ed|s)/visas for employees, and deportation contracts or operations. Add (?!-) after mission. In RELIGION, drop 'family' from the follow list or require that it is not followed by foundation, office or trust.

findings.title: A criminal campaign-finance charge is removed as a 'political donation', and the wire-fraud charge in the same sentence goes with it
findings.scenario: 'Bankman-Fried was charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to make illegal political contributions.' is dropped whole as politics. The red flag is lost from the quote, and the record is lost entirely when it is the only sentence.
findings.fix: Do not apply POLITICS to a sentence that also matches finding.js HIGH (charged, convicted, indicted, pleaded guilty) or that says 'illegal', 'straw donor' or 'campaign finance violation'. The excluded category is donation records, not crimes.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: the Bankman-Fried charge sentence was dropped as politics, so the wire-fraud red flag goes with it.
findings.betterFix: Skip POLITICS when the sentence has charged, convicted, indicted, pleaded, sentenced, illegal, straw donor or 'campaign finance violation'. Donation records stay excluded.

findings.title: French, German and Indian phone numbers and spelled-out emails without brackets are not redacted
findings.scenario: cleanSentences returned these unchanged: 'Call her at +33 1 42 68 53 00', 'Reach him on +49 30 12345678', 'Her mobile is 06 12 34 56 78', 'Office line +91 98765 43210' and 'Email jane dot doe at gmail dot com'. Sources include French, EU and Indian registers and press.
findings.fix: Add a rule for a + country code followed by 6 to 14 digits in groups of 1 to 5. Add the FR form 0[1-9]( \d\d){4}. When the text before the digits says call, phone, mobile, tel or line, accept any run of 8 or more digits with spaces. Add the spelled-out email form '<word> (dot <word>)* at <word> dot (com|org|net|io|co…)'.
findings.evidence: Probe: all five lines came back unchanged.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: all five lines came back unchanged. The phone rules assume 3-4 digit groups or 10-12 digit runs. The spelled-out email form is not handled.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Add +CC followed by 6-14 digits in 1-5 digit groups, the FR form 0[1-9]( \d\d){4}, and digit runs of 8 or more after call/phone/mobile/tel/line. Guard against 9-digit SIREN numbers ('123 456 789') and year runs. Add the spelled-out 'x dot y at z dot com' email form.

findings.title: Birth-year and age shapes get through: '1984-born', 'born in the spring of 1984', 'turned 40', '40th birthday', 'Doe (44)'
findings.scenario: cleanSentences returned these unchanged: 'Doe, a 1984-born entrepreneur, founded Acme.', 'Doe was born in the spring of 1984 in Lyon.', 'He celebrated his 40th birthday in Ibiza.', 'Doe turned 40 last year.' and 'Doe (44) founded Acme.' (the bracketed bare age common in UK and German press). Rule 3 bans dates of birth, including the year.
findings.fix: Add rules for: YEAR-born; born in/during the (spring|summer|autumn|fall|winter|early|late) of YEAR; turned \d{2}; \d{1,3}(st|nd|rd|th) birthday; and a bracket holding only 1[89]-99 right after a capitalised name.
findings.evidence: Probe: each sentence came back with removed {}.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: all five sentences were kept. The DOB rules need a 'born' or 'DOB' lead directly before the date, and there is no age rule for 'turned 40', '(44)' or 'Nth birthday'.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Add YEAR-born, 'born in the (season|early|late) of YEAR', 'turned \d{2}', and Nth birthday. Add a bracketed bare age 1[89]-99 after a capitalised name; do not catch '(2019)' or a footnote '(4)'.

findings.title: cleanData lets through 'born', 'yearOfBirth', 'monthOfBirth', 'nationality' and 'countryOfResidence' fields
findings.scenario: cleanData({person:{born:'March 1984', nationality:'British', countryOfResidence:'England'}, yearOfBirth:1984, monthOfBirth:3}) kept all of them. 'March 1984' has no 'born' lead, and numbers are returned before any key check. Today's sources say they never read these fields, so this is defense in depth only, but a future connector's data would reach the page.
findings.fix: Extend PERSONAL_KEY with born, (year|month|date|place)Of(Birth|Death), nationalit(y|ies), citizenship, countryOfResidence, residence and address (outside register entries). Run the key check before the number and boolean early return.
findings.evidence: Probe output: data.person.born, nationality, countryOfResidence, yearOfBirth and monthOfBirth were all kept.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced: born, nationality, countryOfResidence, yearOfBirth and monthOfBirth were all kept. Numbers return before any key check, and PERSONAL_KEY lacks these names. Defense in depth only.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. Extend PERSONAL_KEY with born, (year|month|date|place)Of(Birth|Death), nationalit(y|ies), citizenship and countryOfResidence. Since the key check already runs in the object branch before walk, numbers are covered once the keys are added; no reordering is needed.

findings.title: publicReport does not strip ifRightPerson entries, so gradeText, score and matchFixed reach the page despite finding.js saying deep.js strips them
findings.scenario: report.js line 903 builds ifRightPerson entries as {...lead, ...}, a full finding that includes gradeText (up to 1,500 characters of cleaned grading text, often more than the 700-character quote). publicReport maps redFlags, companyMatters, possibleNamesake, sections and claimChanges through strip, but not ifRightPerson. The text has been cleaned, but it is an internal field the page was promised never to see.
findings.fix: Add ifRightPerson: (report.ifRightPerson || []).map(strip) in publicReport, and add a test that walks the public report and asserts that no gradeText, score, via or matchFixed key appears at any depth.
findings.verifyNote: Read the code: report.js line 911 pushes {...lead} entries (including gradeText, score and via) into ifRightPerson. publicReport at deep.js line 215 never maps ifRightPerson through strip, so the internal fields reach DeepCheck.js. The text is already privacy-cleaned, so the severity is low.
findings.betterFix: Add ifRightPerson: (report.ifRightPerson || []).map(strip). Better still, strip generically: walk every array of findings in the report, nested 'more' entries included. Add a test asserting that no gradeText, score, via or matchFixed key appears at any depth.
